content_blocks.title: Practice reasoning
content_blocks.text: The Iris dataset makes the supervised workflow small enough to inspect: features are numeric measurements, and the target is a species label. For fitted and unfitted estimators, keep the problem definition, data selection, estimator configuration, and evaluation criterion explicit. When results are uncertain, compare a baseline and inspect examples rather than treating one metric as a complete explanation.

content_blocks.code:
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score
X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=y)
model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X_train, y_train)
print("test accuracy:", round(accuracy_score(y_test, model.predict(X_test)), 3))

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Check input shapes, target alignment, data types, missing values, label order, and whether the expected output assumes a fixed random seed. Fit learned preprocessing only on training data, preferably inside a Pipeline. Do not select parameters by repeatedly looking at the final test set.
